What is Japanese Art?

Japanese art is a broad tradition spanning centuries of painting, printmaking and calligraphy, defined by a philosophy of simplicity, harmony with nature and the beauty of empty space — a concept known as 'ma'. Ink wash painting (sumi-e) is one of its most recognised forms, using black ink in fluid, expressive brushstrokes to suggest landscapes, mountains, trees and water with minimal detail. The style places enormous value on what is left unpainted as much as what is drawn, creating a sense of calm and stillness that translates powerfully into modern interior design. Today, Japanese art wall art prints bring that same meditative quality into contemporary homes and offices, often blended with Japandi aesthetics — a fusion of Japanese and Scandinavian design sensibilities — to create spaces that feel quietly beautiful and uncluttered.

How to Hang Japanese Art Prints in a Home Office

1. Choose your wall: Pick a wall you face regularly — behind your desk or directly opposite your chair works best. A clear, uncluttered wall lets the ink wash artwork breathe and keeps that zen, calming feeling intact.

2. Plan the layout before you hang: Lay all three prints on the floor in front of the wall first. For a set of three, a horizontal row works beautifully — aim for even gaps of around 5–8 cm between each print so the flowing black brushwork reads as one connected landscape.

3. Find the right height: The centre of each print should sit at roughly eye level when you are seated at your desk — usually around 120–130 cm from the floor. This makes the art feel connected to you while you work rather than floating above your eyeline.

4. Consider the wall colour: White, off-white, pale grey or muted sage all pair brilliantly with the black and white palette of these prints. The warm gold-toned sun becomes a natural focal point against any of these backgrounds.

5. Step back and adjust: Once you've made your marks with a pencil, step back to the far side of the room and check the spacing looks balanced from a distance before you commit. A spirit level is your best friend here for keeping everything straight.

Choosing Your Japanese Art Print Format — Which Option Is Right for You?

Finish — Unframed print: print only, ready for you to frame yourself. Framed print: arrives ready to hang. Wrapped canvas: arrives ready to hang, no border, artwork wraps the edges.

Hanging — Unframed print: you source and fit your own frame. Framed print: fully ready to hang straight out of the box. Wrapped canvas: fully ready to hang straight out of the box.

Look on the wall — Unframed print: depends on the frame you choose. Framed print: clean, classic presentation. Wrapped canvas: bold, frameless, gallery-style look.

Paper / material choice — Unframed print: Luster art paper or Museum quality paper. Framed print: Luster art paper or Museum quality paper. Wrapped canvas: canvas material (size options available).

Best for — Unframed print: those who already have a frame or love choosing their own. Framed print: anyone who wants convenience and a polished finish. Wrapped canvas: a contemporary, minimal look that suits Japandi and modern office spaces perfectly.
